cron-fail-closed.ref: TWO CRONS, NO SCHEDULE CHANGE — both stop publishing fabricated numbers, and one of the three defects fixed here was mine from #1435. No job is added, removed, or re-tiered; every tier, interval, oncePerShopDay claim and gate is untouched.  1 · weeklyRevenueDigest — MARGIN WAS STILL FABRICATED AFTER #1435. That PR guarded on `costDetailCount > 0`, which is too weak: with ONE covered invoice out of 32 it still divided that invoice's parts by the FULL week's revenue and would have rendered ~99% — a fabrication with a guard in front of it. Margin is now computed over the covered subset only (coveredRevenue/coveredParts), and the rendered line quotes the COVERED parts/labor so the figures beside the margin share its basis; when coverage is partial the line names it ('on the 9/32 invoices carrying cost detail'). This matches the fill-guard already in services/engines/operations.ts rather than inventing a second pattern.  2 · revenue-reconciliation — HAS BEEN REPORTING $0 IN PROD. cron_log, last 8 days: '$0, 0 jobs' on 7 of them, against actual paid days of $806.75 / $1,554.95 / $3,772.22 / $2,873.28 / $2,008.96. Cause A: it called getDailyRevenueTruth() with NO argument — today so far — while sitting in the 24h tier whose phase follows pod boot (the ROS-081 class), so it fired at 11:59 / 14:03 / 16:01 / 19:08 / 21:18 UTC = 08:00-17:00 ET, before the day's invoices existed. Cause B, and the one that makes it harmful rather than merely wrong: nickMemory.remember() dedupes by CONTENT HASH, so every identical $0 message collapsed onto a single row — nick_memory_insight_e8bb1cbd7719 now carries **813 uses at confidence 1.0**, i.e. 'the shop made $0' is the most-reinforced revenue memory Nick holds, while real days sit at 1-6 uses. Repetition of a bug outvoted the truth. Fixed: reads the PREVIOUS COMPLETE shop day resolved in BUSINESS.timezone (not the container's UTC), stamps the date into the memory content so days can never pile up again, and writes NOTHING when the day has 0 jobs — a $0 day is a closed shop or a broken import, never a 'verified number'. FAIL-CLOSED BY DIRECTION: the job can now only ever write fewer, more-specific memories than before.  3 · getDailyRevenueTruth — published 100.0% margin every single day for 10 consecutive days (recomputed from prod), same root cause as #1435: ALG cost detail dead since 2026-04-09. Given the same subset-basis guard; grossMargin/grossMarginPercent are now nullable and the no-DB fallback returns null instead of a 0% margin, so a failed read cannot read as a measured one.  EVIDENCE: 31 tests (weeklyRevenueDigest 27, previousShopDay 4). MUTATION-VERIFIED ONE AT A TIME, each confirmed applied by grepping its anchor first and each source restored byte-identical after: (a) margin dividing by total revenue instead of coveredRevenue -> 1 failed / 26 passed; (b) quoting shop-wide parts beside the subset margin -> 1 failed; (c) printing zero-valued demand channels -> 1 failed; (d) resolving the reconciliation day in container TZ instead of shop TZ -> 1 failed / 3 passed. Broader surface: 16 files / 145 tests green across server/cron plus revenueAttribution, auto-invoice and adminPermissionCoverage. tsc --noEmit and typecheck:raw both 0 errors. Live re-preview after the fix renders the ALG-gap warning, a 1-entry top-services list, and 'Demand: 3 leads'.  NOT CLAIMED: the ALG importer is still broken — though its root cause is now IDENTIFIED, not unknown. Diagnosed from our own mirror and probe log with zero ALG contact: partsCost, laborCost AND taxAmount all fell to 0 together (2026-03: 77/110/67 of 134 -> 2026-04: 24/24/25 of 143 -> 2026-05: 0/0/0 of 104) while algTicketId and vehicleInfo stayed 100% populated. The three dead fields are exactly the flat line-item money fields mapRawInvoice reads (shopDriverMirror.ts:559-561); the two survivors are exactly what the code's own Wave-99 comment says /api/ticket/listRecentTickets returns. That endpoint is FIRST in the list and 'first one that returns data wins; we don't fall through', so the mirror is fed by a SUMMARY endpoint carrying no line-item split, and `!= null ? ... : 0` writes 0 silently. Wave-99's own probe (scripts/_archive/diagnose-line-items.ts) placed the line items on /api/ticket/listTicketSessions, which the import never reaches. The fix requires a per-ticket detail fetch — extra ALG traffic that collides with SHOP-PROTECT (scheduler.ts:517, probes evict the shop's login) — so it stays an operator decision, now with a price tag instead of a mystery. A warning block at the mapper and a full write-up in docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md prevent the next reader from re-deriving it. The 813-use poisoned memory row also STILL EXISTS — deleting it is a prod write and an operator decision. Neither cron has yet run in production under this change. Both recorded in docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md. Prior entry (#1435 margin fix) superseded per the rolling-manifest rule.

THE UNDERLYING PRODUCTION FACT, probed live and independently of this job: ALG invoice cost detail stopped arriving on 2026-04-09. Of 2,899 lifetime paid invoices, 1,886 carry partsCost and 1,871 carry laborCost — but 0 of the last 30 do. Monthly withParts: Mar 77/134, Apr 24/143, May 0/104, Jun 0/123, Jul 0/106, Aug 0/30. serviceDescription is degrading on the same curve (Jun 31/123, Jul 12/106, Aug 1/30). With partsCost pinned at 0, `revenue - partsCost` equals revenue, so the naive margin formula returns exactly 100% — for a tire shop that plainly buys parts.  FAIL-CLOSED, APPLIED TO DATA RATHER THAN TO ERRORS. The existing failure posture (any thrown query suppresses the whole send; ER_BAD_FIELD/TABLE/PARSE reports SCHEMA BUG) is unchanged and still covered, including the late-query cases added last commit. What this diff adds is the same principle one level up: a query that SUCCEEDS and returns nothing must not render as good news. marginPct is now null unless costDetailCount > 0, the text names the gap ('Parts/labor missing on all N invoices — margin unavailable (ALG import gap)') instead of printing a number, partial coverage is labelled 'cost detail on N/M', and top services queries only described rows and says 'unavailable' when there are none rather than ranking the absence of data.  EVIDENCE: 5 tests added (23 total, up from 18) — margin never rendered at zero cost detail (asserts the string 'Margin' is ABSENT, not merely different), partial-coverage labelling, top-services unavailable line, description-coverage display, and a compute-layer test that marginPct is null on the exact prod shape (32 invoices, $16,656.95, 0 cost detail). Re-running the live preview post-fix renders the warning line and a 1-entry top-services list with '(described: 1/32)'.  NOT CLAIMED, and this is the important part: THE IMPORTER IS NOT FIXED. Why ALG stopped sending parts/labor/description is unknown; ALG is read-only by operator directive so diagnosing it is not this PR's to do. Recorded in docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md as an operator call, together with the note that getDailyRevenueTruth and the parts-percent outlier scan in services/engines/operations.ts consume the same columns and have NOT been reviewed — they may be publishing the same artifact. cron-fail-closed-superseded-1433.ref: THIS DIFF ADDS NO JOB AND REMOVES NONE — it changes what ONE existing cron READS. weeklyRevenueDigest (added #1427, has never fired; first firing Mon 2026-08-10 ET) gains two demand queries: lead rows, and a funnel count over bookings + callback_requests. The schedule entry in cron/scheduler.ts is untouched — same hourly tier, same oncePerShopDay claim, same shop-TZ Monday gate. No job gains the ability to run and none loses it.  THE FAIL-CLOSED CLAIM, AND WHY THE NEW QUERIES CHANGE ITS SHAPE. The two additions run FIFTH and SIXTH, after all four revenue queries have already succeeded. That creates a partial-result hazard the job did not have when every query was about money: revenue would render correctly while the demand line silently read `0 leads · 0 bookings · 0 callbacks` — which on a phone reads as a DEAD WEEK, not as a failed read. That is strictly worse than sending nothing, and it is the exact 'all-clear on failure' class this repo has paid for repeatedly. Both queries therefore sit inside the same try that wraps computeWeeklyRevenueDigest, so any throw suppresses the ENTIRE send and writes the reason to cron_log; the #1125 schema-error taxonomy (ER_BAD_FIELD/TABLE/PARSE -> 'SCHEMA BUG') applies at any query position, not just the first.  EVIDENCE — and the previous test file did NOT cover this. The pre-existing failure test rejected the FIRST query, which proves nothing about a throw that happens after four successes. Two tests added: (1) the 5th query (lead rows) throws after four successes -> sendTelegram not called, recordsProcessed 0, details 'digest failed'; (2) the 6th query (funnel) throws ER_BAD_FIELD_ERROR -> reported as SCHEMA BUG, proving the taxonomy does not degrade with query position.  MUTATION-VERIFIED, and the mutation is the precise regression these guard: wrapping the lead query in a local try/catch that swallows the error and leaves leads=0 — i.e. someone 'defensively' making the demand line resilient — turns test (1) RED (1 failed / 17 passed) while everything else stays green. The mutation was confirmed APPLIED by grepping its anchor before the run (a mutation that silently fails to apply looks exactly like a passing test), and the source was restored byte-identical afterwards: md5 c1fce572c980e4b08e6d148db8dc0b7e on both the backup and the restored file, 18/18 green after restore.  Also verified: the demand line reuses the SHARED countActionableLeads rather than COUNT(*), so this cron cannot drift from dailyReport's lead definition — pinned by a 4-row fixture containing one callback-linked duplicate that must yield 3.  NOT CLAIMED: no production run. The job has never executed; every assertion above is against fixtures and a mutation, not a live Monday send. operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — a three-line overnight summary at the top of /admin (Today), above the decision inbox. It was written months ago, is referenced by a truth-guard test, and had NEVER been mounted. Nothing else on the page moves.  ★ HOW IT WAS FOUND, AND WHY IT NEARLY WENT THE OTHER WAY. The reachability sweep listed MorningBrief.tsx among 8 unreachable page files and it was DELETED — then the suite went red with ENOENT, because server/adminTruth.test.ts opens that component's SOURCE FILE BY PATH and asserts on its text (F25e: live requires online === true, undefined is its own state). A file can be consumed three ways — imported, referenced by symbol, or read by path — and both an import graph and a symbol grep miss the third. It was restored, and the standing question recorded then ('unmounted yet pinned by a truth guard: wire it or retire it WITH its guard, never silently') is what this diff answers. Wired, not deleted.  ONE DEFINITION, TWO CONSUMERS. The brief needs the urgent-lead count, which lived inline inside the 'Urgent leads' SummaryCard JSX. Passing it to the brief would have meant re-typing the predicate — !isCallbackDuplicateLead && ACTIVE_LEAD_STATUSES.has(status) && urgencyScore >= 4 — and a re-typed predicate is exactly how the weekly digest nearly drifted from the daily report on the lead count, which is why countActionableLeads became a shared function instead of two SQL predicates. Extracted to one `urgentLeadCount` useMemo that BOTH the card and the brief read, so the header cannot disagree with the page it introduces. The memo sits ABOVE the isLoading early return; `lint:hooks` (audit-hook-after-return) passes, which is the check that would have caught it otherwise.  DEGRADES BY DESIGN: the component self-suppresses when there is no real signal (no yesterday data -> 'Quiet start'; no overnight activity -> line skipped entirely), so a dead morning renders less, never a fabricated all-clear.  ─── ALSO IN THIS DIFF: the PII linter blind spot, closed and RED-GREEN PROVEN ─── lint-pii's console rule used `[^)]*`, which cannot span a closing paren, so ANY PII interpolation following a call on the same line was invisible. The leak that shipped past it: console.log(`inv ${String(p.invoiceId).padEnd(7)} "${p.name}" ... ${p.phone}`) — a full name AND a full phone — while the weaker sibling statement on the next line, with no inner call, was caught. The rule was scoring the easy half. Widened `[^)]*` -> `[^;]*`: reaches across parens, still stops at a statement boundary so a match cannot run away into an unrelated statement.  THE WIDENING SURFACED 8, AND THEY WERE NOT ALL REAL — 5 raw leaks and 3 already-masked diagnostics (`***${String(caller).slice(-4)}`). A gate that flags correct code is a gate the next person learns to ignore, so the rule now sets `maskable: true`, joining the convention the log-field rules already use via MASKED_VALUE_SIGNAL. The 5 real ones were fixed by REMOVING redundancy rather than blanket-masking: two lines already carried the invoice id (and one the alg_estimates id), so the customer name was duplicate identification and was dropped; two phone prints were reduced to last-4.  ONE WAIVER, AND IT NEEDED A MECHANISM. `backfill-invoice-phone-from-customer.mjs:233` prints two customer names side by side under the heading 'given-name misses (surname exists — inspect before trusting)'. Masking that field does not protect anyone; it prints two rows of asterisks and decides nothing. There was no line-level waiver in this linter — only value allowlists — so one was added: `// pii-allow: <reason>`, with the reason REQUIRED so an empty marker silences nothing. Waived by SIGNATURE, never by filename.  RED-GREEN, BOTH DIRECTIONS: planting the exact original blind-spot shape (a `.padEnd()` call before the PII) INSIDE the very file that carries the waiver turns the audit red and prints the planted line — proving simultaneously that the widened rule catches the class it was widened for, and that the waiver is line-scoped rather than quietly file-scoped, which is the property a file exclusion would have destroyed. Probe removed; audit back to `clean (780 files scanned)`.  EVIDENCE: tsc --noEmit 0 errors; lint:hooks 'no hook-after-early-return patterns detected'; lint:pii clean (780 files); full serial suite green including adminTruth.test.ts, the guard that caught the deletion.  NOT CLAIMED: no browser screenshot of /admin with the brief mounted, and no live morning has rendered it — the composition and its degradation paths are asserted by the component's existing guard, not by a dawn run. Also NOT done in this diff and deliberately so: SMS_CONSENT_GATE was NOT armed. The operator authorised arming, but a read-only prod count taken first shows only 5 of 2,238 customer phone numbers carry an sms.opt_in row (0.2%), so arming would silence marketing SMS to 2,233 customers. That number is the whole reason the gate shipped in shadow, and it belongs in front of the decision rather than behind it. Prior entry (andon ramp) superseded per the rolling-manifest rule.  ─── PRIOR DIFF, SUPERSEDED ─── WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — the admin's red / amber / green finally read at the same brightness, and money columns stop going ragged. This is a VISIBLE change and the only one in the diff; the customer site is untouched.  ★ THE DEFECT, MEASURED FROM TAILWIND'S OWN TOKENS. Tailwind's palette is perceptually uniform WITHIN a hue and not ACROSS hues. At the shades this console actually uses — 1,881 occurrences across 52 distinct shades — its shipped OKLCH lightness reads: red-400 70.4%, emerald-400 76.5%, amber-400 82.8%; red-500 63.7%, emerald-500 69.6%, amber-500 76.9%. That is a 12.4-point lightness spread at ONE nominal step, running BACKWARDS: amber renders brightest, red dimmest. On a shop-floor andon board the colour meaning 'stop, money is at risk' was the quietest thing on the screen and 'caution' pulled the eye first. Equal step numbers were doing unequal work, and no component was wrong — the palette was.  THE FIX, AND WHY IT TOUCHES NO COMPONENT. Tailwind v4 compiles utilities to a var() lookup — verified in the shipped bundle: `.text-red-400{color:var(--color-red-400)}` — and custom properties inherit. So re-tinting the nine tokens on `.admin-shell` re-tints all 1,881 existing call sites at once, with zero component edits and zero sweep risk. Deleting the block restores stock Tailwind exactly; there is no migration to unwind. Scoped to the admin shell deliberately: the customer site keeps stock Tailwind, so no public page pixel moves.  CHROMA IS COMPUTED, NOT EYEBALLED. Each value sits inside its hue's maximum sRGB chroma at that tier's lightness, found by converting OKLCH -> Oklab -> linear sRGB and binary-searching the ceiling per hue. This matters because an out-of-gamut colour is silently clamped by the browser, and clamping shifts lightness — it would have reintroduced the exact drift being removed. The computation is also why the tiers sit at L 0.80 / 0.72 / 0.66 rather than higher: red's chroma ceiling COLLAPSES as lightness rises (0.191 at L70 down to 0.114 at L80), so equalising high would have bleached the one colour that must stay urgent. Red therefore keeps the most chroma at the text tier — severity now leads on saturation, which is a chosen signal, instead of on lightness, which was an accident.  TYPOGRAPHY: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on admin `table/th/td`. Proportional digits make a currency column ragged and make a figure jitter as it re-renders. Applied wholesale to admin tables rather than per-component because a grid where only some columns align is worse than one where none do; 28 files already used it ad hoc, so this makes the rule uniform instead of partial.  EVIDENCE: client/src/__tests__/andon-ramp.test.ts, 8 tests, all green. It asserts the MECHANISM, not the literals — every tier is equal-lightness, tiers descend soft->text->fill, every colour is inside sRGB (same conversion re-implemented in the test so a bad edit cannot pass), red holds the most chroma at the text tier, and the tabular-nums rule exists. MUTATION-VERIFIED: raising amber-400 from L 0.72 to 0.78 turns exactly one test red and the message names the drift — 'tier 400 lightness values: 0.72, 0.78, 0.72'. Source restored and re-run green (8/8) before commit. BUNDLE-VERIFIED: the built CSS carries `.admin-shell{--color-red-400:oklch(72% .17 22.216);...}` for all nine tokens plus the tabular-nums rule — note the minifier writes `72%` rather than `0.72`, which is why a naive grep for the source spelling finds nothing and is not evidence of absence.  NOT CLAIMED: no browser screenshot and no measured contrast audit against the admin's actual backgrounds. The equal-lightness and in-gamut claims are computed and pinned; how the new tints look against every surface in the console is exactly the kind of thing only the operator's eye settles, so this is the one item worth a glance on the phone. If any signal now reads too hot or too flat, the fix is three numbers in one block. Prior entry (orphaned admin component deletions) superseded per the rolling-manifest rule.  ─── PRIOR DIFF, SUPERSEDED ─── WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — NOTHING, and that is proven rather than asserted. Five admin-only component files are deleted: money/{FormField,KPICard,MiniKPI,MoneyBrief,TireSalesPanel}.tsx. A sixth (today/MorningBrief.tsx) was deleted and then RESTORED when the suite caught it — see the third-instrument note below. None has a public URL, so there is no SEO or customer surface in this diff at all.  ★ THE INSTRUMENT LIED FIRST, AND CATCHING IT IS THE POINT. The first reachability pass string-matched guessed import specifiers and reported 148 of 198 page files as unreachable — including WorkOrdersSection.tsx (56KB), CustomersList.tsx and DeclinedEstimatesSection.tsx, i.e. the entire money cockpit — and found ZERO occurrences of a route declaration in App.tsx. Both were detector bugs: imports are written './pages/About' relative to App.tsx (not '@/pages/About' or './About'), and admin sections are imported by SIBLING admin files rather than by App.tsx. Acting on that output would have deleted the live admin. It was rebuilt as a REAL import graph that parses every specifier and RESOLVES it to a file on disk, then walks reachability from the true entrypoints (App.tsx + main.tsx, tests excluded because a test import does not make a page live). Trust signal: only 2 relative specifiers in the entire client fail to resolve, and the corrected graph finds 190 of 198 pages reachable and 145 route declarations in App.tsx.  EVIDENCE, TWO INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENTS. (1) Resolved import graph: each of the six has zero importers. (2) Repo-wide name grep across client/, server/ and shared/ as the cross-check, which is what disambiguated the near-misses: TireSalesPanel, KPICard and MiniKPI appear in NO file but their own; FormField's only other hit is components/ui/form.tsx, which exports its own unrelated FormField (a name collision, not an import); MoneyBrief's three other hits are all COMMENTS referencing a since-extracted constant (moneyMath.ts, CustomersList.tsx:84, DeclinedEstimatesSection.tsx:14); MorningBrief's other hits are the SERVER cron server/cron/jobs/morningBrief.ts and the sibling Customers/Leads/Outreach brief components, none of which import the client page. Dynamic-by-string loading is ruled out structurally: admin/registry.tsx loads every section with a static lazy(() => import('./X')), which the resolver follows.  INTENT CHECKED, NOT GUESSED. git log on each file: FormField, KPICard, MiniKPI and TireSalesPanel were added 2026-06-01 and NEVER touched again. MoneyBrief and MorningBrief were last touched by repo-wide SWEEP commits (#1336 'admin stops reporting all-clear on reads that failed', #1045 'failure must never render as good news', the U2 rounded-container pass) — maintenance paid on dead code, not evidence anyone meant to wire them. The sibling Customers/Leads/Outreach briefs ARE wired, so this is a partially-orphaned family, not a dormant feature.  ★ TWO DELIBERATE PINS FOUND AND KEPT — the same sweep that produced the delete list also produced a do-not-delete list, and both were named by a pasted mandate as things to 'resolve'. HomeLegacy.tsx (73KB) stays: Home.tsx:10 reads 'vs HomeLegacy (kept as rollback)'. TireFinderLegacy.tsx (116KB) stays: TireFinder.tsx is a 12-line re-export shim whose comment states the legacy page is 'kept as a byte-for-byte rollback + the home of the shared OrderModal, and its own regressions import TireFinderLegacy explicitly' — and TireOrderModal.tsx confirms it was extracted FROM that file. Deleting either would have destroyed a documented rollback path.  ★ THE SUITE CAUGHT A SIXTH DELETION AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL RESULT HERE. MorningBrief.tsx was deleted on two agreeing instruments and the full run went red: server/adminTruth.test.ts opens that component's SOURCE FILE BY PATH and asserts on its text (F25e — live requires online === true), so the failure was ENOENT, the guard could not find what it guards. The name-grep HAD listed adminTruth.test.ts under MorningBrief; I misattributed the hit to the sibling server cron cron/jobs/morningBrief.ts. The evidence was present and misread. GENERALISED: a file can be consumed three ways — imported, referenced by symbol, or READ BY PATH — and both an import graph and a symbol grep miss the third. This repo has a whole family of source-text assertion tests from the ROS-083 'failure must never render as good news' wave, so the pattern is not rare. The file was restored (adminTruth.test.ts back to 13/13) and the remaining five were re-checked by searching for their FILENAME AS A STRING across server/, scripts/ and client/: zero references each. Standing question recorded in the audit doc: MorningBrief is unmounted yet pinned by a truth guard — wire it or retire it WITH its guard, never silently.  NOT CLAIMED: no browser screenshot of /admin/money after the deletion. The zero-render proof is static (two instruments plus the registry's static-import structure); if any admin surface ever loaded one of these six by a runtime-computed path this entry is wrong, and a search for dynamic import of those paths found none. operator-walkthrough-superseded-2026-08-.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — one MORE line in Monday's Telegram digest, and one admin API that was never reachable is gone. So a 'weekly intelligence report' existed in code, was documented, was permission-checked, and had never once run.  WHY THIS IS A COLLAPSE, NOT A DELETION. The tempting read is 'nobody clicked it, nobody wants it'. The evidence says otherwise: it required clicking, and this operator consumes pushed reports (daily SMS, Telegram digests) and no pull-only ones. What went unused was the TRANSPORT, not the content — the same finding that made the revenue digest a push in #1427. So its content moves to the live pushed job: `Demand: N leads · N bookings · N callbacks (N still open)`, where unworked callbacks are the actionable half.  ★ A CONSISTENCY TRAP CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The obvious implementation is `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leads`. That would have made this report DISAGREE with the daily one: dailyReport.ts:48 counts leads through `countActionableLeads` (shared/leadSource.ts), which excludes a `source='callback'` lead carrying a `callbackId` because that row and its callback_requests row are the SAME PERSON. A raw count double-counts them. Re-expressing that predicate in SQL would have forked a definition the repo deliberately centralized, so the digest fetches the rows and calls the shared function — one definition, no drift. A test pins it: a 4-row lead fixture containing exactly one callback-linked duplicate must yield 3, and the comment says out loud that a reading of 4 means someone re-implemented the rule in SQL. WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — nothing on Instagram, which is how this was found. The operator asked why autonomous reels had stopped; production said the rest.  ★ ONE — A BILLING WALL FILED AS A TRANSIENT BLIP. Reel job #1380001 (2026-08-04 18:03, cron) failed with Higgsfield's grace_daily_limit_reached / unlock_full_access_notice. That text matched NONE of the eight classifier patterns — no "billing", no "exhausted", and no "rate" for RATE_LIMIT — so it fell through to UNKNOWN, whose policy is RETRY_BACKOFF and whose operator-facing reason literally reads "unrecognised failure - treated as transient, but review the message". The daily cron re-attempted every day and NOTHING alerted. It now classifies as QUOTA_OR_CREDIT -> PAUSE_PROVIDER, which stops the lane and raises a human.  Deliberately NOT RATE_LIMIT, and the difference is money: RATE_LIMIT is RETRY_WITHOUT_CONSUMING_ATTEMPT, built for a request refused before work began that clears on its own. A grace-tier daily cap does not clear by waiting and cannot be retried out of - it needs a plan upgrade. A test asserts it is not that class.  ★ THE TEST CAUGHT A TRAP IN MY OWN FIX. The first draft appended the new wordings to the existing QUOTA_OR_CREDIT regex, which is wrapped in  ... . `_` is a WORD character, so   never fires inside an underscore-joined token:  grace[_ ]daily[_ ]limit  does NOT match "grace_daily_limit_reached", because the boundary it wants sits between `limit` and `_reached` with word characters on both sides. Three cases went red. The plan-wall patterns are now their own entry and the working credit regex is untouched.  ★ TWO — A TRUNCATED RESPONSE REPORTED AS A BACKTICK. ig_autopost_log carried `Unexpected token '`', "```json
{"... is not valid JSON` (2026-08-05) and `Unterminated string in JSON at position 830` (2026-08-01). Both are ONE root cause - the model's output was cut off mid-object - and neither message says so; the first names the backtick, which is the only detail that does not matter. parseJsonObject now detects an opening brace with no closing one and throws `LLM response truncated before the JSON object closed (N chars received) - raise max_tokens for this call`, and wraps genuine syntax errors instead of leaking the raw parser text into a column the operator reads.  ★ AND A MUTATION PROVED PART OF MY OWN FIX DEAD. The draft also stripped an UNCLOSED fence. Disabling that line changed no behaviour: the brace isolation already recovers the object whenever one closed, and when none closed the truncation branch fires first either way. It was removed rather than kept with a comment claiming it fixed the prod error. The surviving branch is verified load-bearing - disabling it turns 2 cases red.  EVIDENCE: server/providerErrorAndLlmJsonTruth.test.ts (10), built from the EXACT prod stderr payload rather than a paraphrase, MUTATION-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS - removing the plan-wall pattern (3 red) · reclassifying it as RATE_LIMIT (4 red) · disabling the truncation branch (2 red) · deleting the truncation message (1 red). One further mutation SURVIVED and that is why a line was deleted; the first attempt at it silently failed to apply and reported a false pass, so the applied ones are proven by echoing the removed text and by git diff --stat. A regression case pins that the other six error classes are unchanged. Full serial suite: 405 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,981 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean.  NOT CLAIMED: neither fix makes a reel. The Higgsfield account is behind a plan-tier daily cap - an operator billing action - and this change only makes that state stop the lane loudly instead of retrying it silently. No production run has exercised either path since the change; the classification is asserted against the recorded payload, not against a new live failure.

Checked rather than assumed: grepping the ledger for sms / opt-out / consent / tcpa / compliance returns exactly one matching entry, `sms-customer-identity` ('Inbound SMS customer identity resolution + consent'), and this diff changes what that capability DOES. Inventing a new entry would have been the fabricated-capability failure the ledger exists to prevent; deferring would have been false, since the match is real.  WHAT MOVED. `evidence.codeCommit` records the vocabulary collapse and `lastVerifiedAt` advances 2026-07-28 -> 2026-08-09. NO STATE CLAIM CHANGES: operationalState stays `unit_verified` and exposure stays `disabled`, because this diff proves behaviour against tests and source, not against a production inbound STOP. The existing P2 blocker (multi-match frequency unmeasured) is untouched — it is a different question and closing it here would be an unearned claim.  WHAT WAS ADDED TO deferredScope, and this is the honest half: plain-English revocation ('stop texting me', 'take me off this list') is NOT detected. The FCC's April 2025 rule permits revocation by any reasonable method, and no exact-keyword list can cover that. Exact-match on the whole trimmed body is RETAINED deliberately — inbound spam routinely carries a 'Reply STOP' footer, so substring matching would suppress people who never asked, failing in the direction that costs the shop revenue while looking identical to a bug. Recording the limit in deferredScope means the ledger stops implying coverage the code does not have.  THE UNDERLYING CHANGE: the opt-out vocabulary had drifted into three copies — index query 10 words, inbound handler 5, instrumentation 5. Nobody went un-suppressed, since the index re-derives from raw inbound bodies and is the real safety net, but STOPALL / REVOKE / OPT OUT produced no confirmation reply, no sms.opt_out compliance row, and stayed sendable until the 5-minute cache turned over. Now one shared list, with internal whitespace collapsed so 'STOP  ALL' matches. Pinned by server/__tests__/optOutVocabulary.test.ts (7): the JS copies import the constant, and the two SQL literals — which cannot import anything — are parsed out of source and compared, so widening one and forgetting the other fails and NAMES the missing words. render-spend-trajectory.ref: THIS DIFF CHANGES SPEND, and the change is downward and bounded. The rule fires on server/services/reelPipeline.ts, which is where render spend is both reserved and settled, so here is the whole trajectory.  BEFORE: a paid provider returning a verdict no retry can clear (QUOTA_OR_CREDIT, AUTH_INVALID -> PAUSE_PROVIDER) sent the job terminal. Spend for the remaining beats: zero, because nothing rendered - and no reel either. AFTER, and only when REEL_FALLBACK_TO_TEMPLATE_STOCK=true: the remaining beats render on the local ffmpeg lane. Spend for those beats is still zero (reelClipCostUsd('template_stock') is 0 and the lane makes no provider call - templateStockStudio.ts contains exactly one fetch, a download of an already-hosted hero image), and now there IS a reel. No path in this diff can increase spend: the flip is one-way and only ever moves from a paid lane to the free one, never the reverse.  ★ THE REAL FINDING, and it is a defect this change would otherwise have INTRODUCED. Settlement read `clipUrls.length * reelClipCostUsd(videoProvider)`, and the comment directly above it warns that settling at a flat rate is 'what made a mid-flight provider flip undetectable in the ledger, and would settle a free local reel as if it had spent Seedance money'. Introducing a mid-job flip made videoProvider stop being the provider that actually rendered, so a degraded reel would have billed every clip at the paid rate - resurrecting the exact bug already fixed once on the repair lane (#1343, where a hardcoded seedance1_5 filed template_stock repairs under Higgsfield's name). The reserve() call at enqueue anticipates this in writing: 'a mid-flight provider flip can still diverge - settlement is where actuals must be reconciled.' Settlement now splits the bill: paidClips * reelClipCostUsd(videoProvider) + freeLaneClips * reelClipCostUsd('template_stock'), where freeLaneClips counts what the free lane actually rendered this run. With no flip freeLaneClips is 0 and the expression is arithmetically identical to the original, so unflipped jobs settle exactly as before.  The reservation itself is UNTOUCHED: still created at enqueue against the selected provider at beatsCount * reelClipCostUsd(reservedProvider), still checked against the daily ceiling. A degraded job therefore over-reserves and under-settles, which is the conservative direction and the same direction any partially-failed job already takes.  EVIDENCE: server/reelFreeLaneFallback.test.ts (15), MUTATION-VERIFIED FIVE WAYS - dropping the durable-storage assert on the flip (2 red), dropping the opt-in flag gate (2 red), broadening the predicate from PAUSE_PROVIDER to any error (3 red), dropping the beat re-run (2 red), and reverting settlement to flat per-clip billing (1 red). Each mutation script fails loudly if its anchor is absent, because a mutation that does not apply looks exactly like a passing test; the source file was restored byte-identical after every run (sha256 compared, identical=True both times).  Suites: 18 files / 192 passed across every suite importing reelPipeline or socialPipeline. tsc --noEmit clean. Full nickstire pre-commit gate green (routes, hooks, source lint, brand voice, tsc).  NOT CLAIMED: no production run, no live provider call, and no measurement against generation_reservations. The flag is unset in prod, so on merge this diff changes nothing that runs. The free lane has still never published a reel - that P2 blocker stands.
